shortDescription: Brazilian markets rallied on Tuesday as traders pointed to two polls showing right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva were statistically tied in a potential runoff ahead of next month's election.

children: Brazilian markets rallied on Tuesday as traders pointed to two polls showing right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva were statistically tied in a potential runoff ahead of next month's election.
A Nexus poll commissioned by BTG Pactual showed for the first time Bolsonaro slightly ahead of Lula (46% to 45%) in a simulated second-round runoff.
The candidates were tied at 41% each in a separate Quaest poll commissioned by Globo. Both surveys had margins of error of 2 percentage points.
The Brazilian real (BRBY) strengthened about 1% against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday, while benchmark stock index Bovespa
"The polls show it won't be easy for President Lula to win, which is interesting for the market," said Jefferson Rugik, director of Correparti Corretora.
A Bolsonaro win could result in a more austere fiscal policy starting in 2027, said Gabriel Mollo, an investment analyst at Daycoval Corretora.
First-round voting is scheduled for October 4, while a second-round runoff would be held on October 25.
